system.name: Neo
system.one_liner: a hardware accelerator for real-time on-device 3D Gaussian Splatting using reuse-and-update sorting

components.name: DRAM
components.role: off-chip memory supplying Gaussian data and feature/scene data to the accelerator

components.name: Memory Controller
components.role: arbitrates data movement between DRAM and the three on-chip engines

components.name: Preprocess Engine
components.role: performs frustum culling and feature extraction, producing the feature table and incoming Gaussian tables

components.name: Sorting Engine
components.role: performs dynamic partial sorting and sorting of incoming Gaussian tables using parallel Sorting Cores

components.name: Rasterization Engine
components.role: performs subtile-based rasterization and deferred depth updates enabling reuse-and-update sorting

components.name: Sorting Core 1..16
components.role: 16 parallel cores composing the Sorting Engine

components.name: Rasterization Core 1..4
components.role: 4 parallel cores composing the Rasterization Engine

content.key_idea: Neo's accelerator is organized as three pipelined engines (Preprocessing, Sorting, Rasterization) around a shared memory controller and DRAM, with the Sorting and Rasterization engines each internally parallelized into many identical cores.
content.reading_order: Left to right: DRAM feeds the Memory Controller, which connects bidirectionally to the three stacked engines (Preprocessing, Sorting, Rasterization) inside the green Neo Architecture box; dashed lines expand the Sorting and Rasterization engines into their parallel core lists on the right.

Our design consists of three main engines, Preprocessing Engine, Sorting Engine, and Rasterization Engine

summary: This figure gives the top-level architecture of the Neo accelerator for real-time 3D Gaussian Splatting. A Memory Controller sits between off-chip DRAM and the Neo Architecture block, which contains three main engines connected in a pipeline: the Preprocessing Engine (frustum culling and feature extraction, producing feature and incoming-Gaussian tables), the Sorting Engine (dynamic partial sorting and incoming-table sorting), and the Rasterization Engine (subtile-based rasterization with deferred depth updates). Dashed lines expand the Sorting Engine into its 16 parallel Sorting Cores and the Rasterization Engine into its 4 parallel Rasterization Cores, foreshadowing the more detailed microarchitecture figures that follow. The layout is simple and sparse, emphasizing the pipeline of three engines over a green-bordered chip boundary.
summary_zh: 该图展示Neo加速器的顶层架构：DRAM通过内存控制器连接三大引擎——预处理引擎（视锥剔除与特征提取）、排序引擎（动态部分排序与新增高斯排序）、光栅化引擎（子瓦片光栅化与延迟深度更新），虚线展开显示排序引擎含16个并行排序核心，光栅化引擎含4个并行光栅化核心。
